steps: This video shows how to put each enterprise control in its proper place. It starts with a shortcut: the agent runs with bypass permissions and no isolation, so everything not denied runs. That is a big blast radius.
Instead, your code starts a sandboxed worker per task, with a scoped working directory, scoped credentials, and disallowed tools set.
A sensitive tool call leaves the agent, and the pre tool use hook sees it first. It acts as a fast, fail safe policy gateway, and this call passes policy.
Next, can use tool parks the call in an approval queue until a named human approver decides, with a timeout set. The approver approves.
The call now goes through a shared, vetted M C P server that fronts the system, authenticated with O Auth. The result comes back, and it is treated as untrusted data.
The post tool use hook writes the audit entry, and only then does the result reach the agent. Sandbox, hooks, callback and M C P server each handle one concern.

The takeaway: match each concern to the single control that fits it, sandbox for isolation, hooks for policy and audit, the callback for human approval, subagents and M C P for scope. The full walkthrough is in the Gennoor Claude certification course.
